# PhysxSurfaceDeformableMaterialAPI

[PhysX](glossary.md#physx) bend damping for a surface deformable material, read only when the material [prim](glossary.md#prim) also carries OmniPhysicsSurfaceDeformableMaterialAPI and lists PhysxSurfaceDeformableMaterialAPI in its [usd-schemas](prim.md#columns).

- **Applies to:** [`Material`](glossary.md#material)
- **Requires on the same prim:** [`OmniPhysicsSurfaceDeformableMaterialAPI`](OmniPhysicsSurfaceDeformableMaterialAPI.md)
- **Read only when listed in `usd-schemas`.**
- **No builder:** `ovphysx.population` and `Population.hpp` do not write this component; the consumer reads it when another population writes it.

## What USD population writes

Published like any applied physics API: every declared attribute at its resolved value. [USD](glossary.md#usd) population also lists the built-in PhysxDeformableMaterialAPI in usd-schemas. No column is rewritten or created by the producer.

## Columns

*Raw fallback* is the USD schema value. *Producer writes* is what [ovstage](glossary.md#ovstage) population puts in the column for a USD stage. *Parser default* applies on the consumer when the column is absent, in stage units. **diverges** means writing the raw fallback literally parses differently from omitting the column (the parser default): USD population may well publish that very value for an unauthored attribute, so the marker is about the column being present, not about its value.

| Column | Type | Units | Raw fallback | Producer writes | Parser default | If absent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `physxDeformableMaterial:bendDamping` | float32 |  | 0.0 | resolved USD value (authored, else raw fallback) | 0.0 | 0: no bend damping. A negative value is clamped to 0 at parse. |

## Interactions

- **[`OmniPhysicsSurfaceDeformableMaterialAPI`](OmniPhysicsSurfaceDeformableMaterialAPI.md):** Read only when that API is listed on the same prim: it decides whether the material is parsed as a surface material at all.
- **[`PhysxDeformableMaterialAPI`](PhysxDeformableMaterialAPI.md):** elasticityDamping lives on the built-in PhysxDeformableMaterialAPI, which the parser checks separately.
